decision.summary: Tenant wants to replace the broken landlord-supplied LG washing machine with their own. This needs landlord consent, so I asked the landlord, noted the case, put the job on hold to 30 July and updated the tenant.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: At intake, routine. Outstanding: landlord consent to the tenant's own machine, who pays removal and fitting, and what happens to the existing LG.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?

answers.answer: Not from agency staff. The decision belongs to the landlord, because it concerns their appliance and consent to the tenant's own. No escalation.

Send our contractor to inspect/repair the existing machine

args.body: Hi, thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Fitting your own machine needs the landlord's consent, so we've asked them. We've noted that the new machine would stay yours and you'd take it with you when you leave. We've also asked who covers disconnecting the old one and fitting the new one, and what happens to the existing LG. Please don't remove or replace it until we confirm. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We'll update you by 30 July.
